label: Video

fields.name: preset
fields.label: Preset
fields.tooltip: Recipe shortcut — Draft (0.2 MP, 10 steps) for fast prompt/motion iteration (default — pair with the ⚡ Turbo variant for the fastest loop), Final (1.0 MP, 30 steps) for production output. Fills empty fields only; values you've set are preserved.

fields.name: h3_ref_image_size
fields.label: Ref Image Sizing
fields.tooltip: 'match' scales refs to the generation's pixel area (faster). 'max' uses 2048px short edge for best identity fidelity (several times slower — ref tokens ride through every step).

fields.name: h3_attention
fields.label: Attention
fields.tooltip: Attention backend — ONE at a time (all three install the same optimized_attention override; combining them is a silent last-writer-wins). kitchen = comfy-kitchen int8 (core ModelAttentionBackend, v0.32.0+); sol = Sol-Attn block-sparse (kijai/ComfyUI-SolAttn_triton); sage = sageattn (KJNodes PathchSageAttentionKJ, mode auto). Empty = engine default. Legacy h3_sage_attention: true maps to sage.

fields.name: h3_fp16_accumulation
fields.label: FP16 Matmul Accumulation
fields.tooltip: Enable torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_fp16_accumulation. Requires PyTorch 2.7.1+. Small speedup on fp16 matmuls with minimal quality impact. Uses KJNodes ModelPatchTorchSettings.

fields.name: h3_torch_compile
fields.label: Torch Compile DiT
fields.tooltip: torch.compile the H3 DiT with inductor backend. First sampling step is SLOW (compilation); subsequent steps are faster. Best for batch generation where the compile cost amortizes. Uses KJNodes TorchCompileModelAdvanced with compile_transformer_blocks_only=True.

fields.name: guide_scale
fields.label: Guide Scale
fields.tooltip: CFG guidance scale. LTX 2.3 typical: 3.0, Wan: 6.0.

fields.name: guide_strength
fields.label: Director Guide Strength
fields.tooltip: On LTX: LTXDirector guide_strength — controls how strongly keyframe/prompt-relay conditioning steers generation. On Wan VACE: WanVideoVACEEncode strength — how strongly the VACE conditioning image (keyframes, I2V input) influences the output.

fields.name: sampler
fields.label: Sampler
fields.tooltip: ComfyUI core sampler for the LTX KSamplerSelect path. 'euler_cfg_pp' is recommended for LTX flow-matching models (CFG++ samplers are designed for CFG≈1 generation). Not used on Wan VACE (which has its own WanVideoScheduler).

fields.name: scheduler
fields.label: Scheduler
fields.tooltip: ComfyUI core BasicScheduler sigma schedule. 'beta' is the LTX default. 'linear_quadratic' is the scheduler the LTX-Director reference workflow uses. Not used on Wan VACE (see wan_scheduler).

fields.name: shift_video
fields.label: Video Sigma Shift
fields.tooltip: Flow-matching noise schedule shift for the video stream. Higher = more noise earlier (more motion diversity), lower = more noise later (more detail preservation). H3 default: 12.0.

fields.name: shift_audio
fields.label: Audio Sigma Shift
fields.tooltip: Flow-matching noise schedule shift for the audio stream. The DiT derives the full audio schedule from this value + the video shift. H3 default: 3.0.

fields.name: relay_epsilon
fields.label: Relay Epsilon
fields.tooltip: Boundary sharpness for prompt relay. Smaller = crisper transitions between segments, larger = smoother blends. Both LTX (LTXDirector cross-attn mask) and Wan VACE (WanVideoPromptRelay Gaussian penalty) use sigma = 1/ln(1/epsilon).

fields.name: retake_enabled
fields.label: Enable Retake
fields.tooltip: Re-generate a frame range within an existing video. Upload the base video as 'Retake Source', set the frame range, and provide a retake prompt. Frames outside the range are anchored; frames inside are regenerated. On the LTX path this drives LTXDirector's native retake mode via timeline_data JSON (retakeMode/retakeStart/retakeLength). On Wan VACE, apply_retake_mask loads the source via VHS_LoadVideoPath and builds VACE conditioning via WanVideoVACEStartToEndFrame (outside-range anchored, inside-range free). Video source = full retake; image source = single-frame anchor at frame 0 (partial).

fields.name: retake_start_frame
fields.label: Start Frame
fields.tooltip: First frame to regenerate (0-indexed).

fields.name: retake_end_frame
fields.label: End Frame
fields.tooltip: Last frame to regenerate. -1 = final frame.

fields.name: retake_prompt
fields.label: Retake Prompt
fields.tooltip: Prompt that drives regeneration in the retake range. Empty = reuse the global prompt.

fields.name: retake_strength
fields.label: Retake Strength
fields.tooltip: Retake influence strength. 1.0 = nominal regeneration, lower = subtler, >1.0 = amplified. On LTX: drives LTXDirector's retake guide strength. On Wan VACE: maps to VACE conditioning strength in the retake frame range.

fields.name: upscale_enabled
fields.label: Enable Hi-Res Pass
fields.tooltip: Run a second diffusion pass at 2× resolution after the base generation. On LTX: the LTXV spatial upscaler model upsamples the latent, then a short refinement sampler adds detail. On Wan VACE: spatial latent interpolation (bislerp) + WanVideoSampler v2v refine pass (denoise_strength). Costs ~30% extra time + VRAM. Off = single-pass at base resolution.

fields.name: upscale_steps
fields.label: Refine Steps
fields.tooltip: Sampler steps in the hi-res refinement pass. Fewer than the base pass — the upscaled latent already carries structure; this just adds detail. Typical: 6–12.

fields.name: upscale_denoise
fields.label: Refine Denoise
fields.tooltip: How much to perturb the upscaled latent before refining. 0.0 = locked (no change), 0.3 = detail boost (typical), 0.6 = significant reinterpretation. Above 0.6 risks losing the original composition. On Wan VACE this drives WanVideoSampler's denoise_strength (v2v mode).

fields.name: upscale_cfg
fields.label: Refine CFG
fields.tooltip: Classifier-free guidance for the refinement pass. Lower = more faithful to the upscaled latent; higher = prompt-driven reshaping. Default 1.0 (gentle).

fields.label: Format

sections.label: Official guide (vendored verbatim)
sections.body: Authoritative guide vendored at docs/prompt-guides/minimax-h3/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_base_en.md (T2VA / I2VA / FL2VA / L2VA) and VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_ref_en.md (Ref2VA), copied verbatim from MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 on 2026-08-05 (same bytes as the upstream h3-prompt-writing skill's references/, served to the agent via the bundle's h3_prompt_library tool). Follow those docs exactly — §2 (Final Prompt Structure), §3 (keyframes per task variant), §4 (how to write the three core fields).

sections.label: Three core fields (from §2.2)
sections.body: integrated_multimodal_description: visuals, actions, shots, speakers, dialogue, singing, diegetic audio along the timeline. overall_soundscape: ambient sound, physical action sounds, non-verbal human sounds across the whole video. non_diegetic_music: background music the characters cannot hear.

sections.label: Native shot + instruction notation (§2.1, §4.2)
sections.body: Multi-shot is native: [Shot 1] gets no timestamp; later shots open "[Shot 2] At 00:03.500, the camera cuts to ..." with strictly increasing cut times inside the duration. With keyframes the mode instruction line comes FIRST — FL2VA: "How the reference pictures align with the target video — Picture 1 (from Shot 1) aligns with the 0.00-second mark; Picture 2 (from Shot N) aligns with the S.SS-second mark" (S.SS = duration, two decimals); I2VA: "For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced."; L2VA aligns <Picture 1> with the final-second mark. Dialogue: <d>[Language] the line.</d>.

sections.label: Specs (from model card)
sections.body: Duration 4–15 s (124–362 frames at 24 fps). Aspect: 21:9, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 9:16. Shorter side ≈ 768 px (2K needs H3-Regenerate-2K). Audio: 32 kHz stereo. 11 stable languages (en, zh, ja, ko, ar, fr, de, it, pt, ru, es).

enhance_prompt:
You are a MiniMax H3 video prompting expert. Rewrite the user's rough prompt into H3's native three-field prompt format (official T2VA/I2VA/FL2VA/L2VA guide, vendored at docs/prompt-guides/minimax-h3/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_base_en.md).

- Identify the mode from the conditioning the user describes (guide §2.1): T2VA = no keyframes; I2VA = first-frame image; FL2VA = first + last frames (this card's head route); L2VA = last-frame image. The instruction line differs per mode; the three core fields are the same for all.
- T2VA: no instruction line — begin directly with the three core fields.
- I2VA first line, verbatim: 'For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.' Then establish the image's style, subjects, composition, and scene anchors before developing forward (guide §3.1).
- FL2VA first line, verbatim: 'How the reference pictures align with the target video — Picture 1 (from Shot 1) aligns with the 0.00-second mark of the target video; Picture 2 (from Shot N) aligns with the S.SS-second mark of the target video.' S.SS = total duration to two decimals; N = the last shot's index. Then describe the continuous first-to-last path — a SINGLE shot unless the user explicitly asked for more (guide §3.2).
- L2VA first line, verbatim: 'How the reference pictures align with the target video — <Picture 1> (from [Shot N]) aligns with the S.SS-second mark of the target video.' Then infer a plausible opening that converges onto the supplied final frame (guide §3.3).
- One blank line after the instruction line (when present), then the three labeled fields in order (guide §2.2):
-   integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] <style at the shot start — Live-action/cinematic, 2D-animated, 3D CG, claymation, watercolor... — then composition, subjects, actions, camera, dialogue, diegetic sound along the timeline>
-   overall_soundscape: 1-4 sentences on ambient sound, physical action sounds, and non-verbal human sounds (wind, footsteps, breathing); N/A only when the user wants total silence. Never repeat dialogue, singing, or music here.
-   non_diegetic_music: 1-3 sentences on score instrumentation, speed, rhythm, and dynamic changes — concrete, no mood words; N/A when there is none. Music the characters can hear (radio, sung vocals) is diegetic and belongs in the multimodal description.
- Shots (guide §4.2): [Shot 1] gets NO timestamp; later shots open '[Shot 2] At 00:03.500, the camera cuts to ...' — cut times strictly increasing and inside the requested duration.
- Camera (guide §4.3): motion type + amplitude + speed written as a natural action — 'The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward the folded letter in her hands.'
- Dialogue/singing (guide §4.4): introduce the speaker, then '<d>[Language] the line.</d>'; on-screen text (guide §4.5) quoted verbatim, untranslated.
- Every detail must be visible or audible at its point on the timeline; timing matches the requested duration (4-15 s at 24 fps).

MiniMax H3 is a JOINT video+audio model — one prompt conditions both
the video track and the audio track. This is H3's NATIVE structured
format, not generic single-take video prose.

## Native format rules
- Multi-shot timelines are CORRECT here: '[Shot 1] ... [Shot 2] At
  00:03.500, the camera cuts to ...' The first shot gets no timestamp;
  later shots open with a strictly increasing cut time inside the
  requested duration.
- Camera motion is a natural action combining motion type + amplitude +
  speed: "The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward
  the folded letter in her hands." (Zoom In/Out, Push In/Pull Out, Pan,
  Truck, Tilt, Pedestal, Arc, Tracking, Static, Shake, POV, Roll.)
- Dialogue/singing: introduce the speaker first, then write the line as
  '<d>[Language] the line.</d>'. Visible on-screen text goes in double
  quotes, verbatim and untranslated.
- Every detail must be visible or audible at its point on the timeline —
  concrete specifics over abstract words like "cinematic" or "beautiful".

## Hard constraints
- The described timeline must match the requested duration (4-15 s at
  24 fps) — never timing that runs past the video length.
- NEVER emit image-prompt tokens ("8K", "masterpiece", "best quality",
  "highly detailed") or other-model sampler syntax ("score_9", "dpm++").
- Emit the labeled fields as plain 'field: content' lines — no markdown
  headings, no bullet lists inside the fields.


    ## Output format — STRICT
    Return ONLY a single JSON object. No markdown fences, no explanation,
    no text before or after. The whole response must be parseable by
    JSON.parse.

    Schema:
      {"positive": "<your output>", "negative": ""}

    Rules:
    - "positive" is always filled with your output per the instructions above.
    - "negative" is always the empty string "".
    - Both values are plain strings. Escape inner quotes and newlines per JSON.
    - Never wrap the whole response in extra quotes.
